sanskrit: asthād dyaur asthāt pṛthivy asthād viśvam idaṃ jagat | tiṣṭhanti parvatā ime sthāmann aśvā araṃsata ||
english: Heaven has stood firm, earth has stood firm, this entire world has stood firm. These mountains stand steady; in their steadiness the horses have found rest.

sanskrit: ya udānaḍ vyāyane ya udānaṭ parāyaṇe | āvartanaṃ nivartanaṃ yo gopā api taṃ huve ||
english: Him who raises up at going forth, who raises up at the final journey, the one who is the guardian of return and of coming back — him too I call upon.

sanskrit: āvṛto nyāvṛto 'bhyavartanam āyanam | agneś catasra āvṛtas tābhiṣ ṭvā tarpayāmasi ||
english: The turnings, the counter-turnings, the return-course, the approach — the four turnings of Agni: with these we satisfy you.

sanskrit: jātavedo ni vartaya śataṃ te santv āvṛtaḥ sahasraṃ ta upāvṛtaḥ | tābhir enaṃ ni vartaya ||
english: O Jātavedas, turn him back. Let there be a hundred turnings for you, a thousand counter-turnings for you. With these, turn him back.

sanskrit: adārasṛd bhavatu deva soma- -asmin yajñe maruto mṛḍatā naḥ | mā no vidad abhibhā mo aśastir mā naḥ prāpad ducchunā dveṣyā yā ||
english: Let the one who tears asunder be powerless, O god Soma. Be gracious to us, O Maruts, in this sacrifice. Let not oppression find us, let not ill-omen reach us; let not the hateful misfortune reach us.

sanskrit: yo adya daivyo vadho jighāṃsan na upāyati | yuvaṃ taṃ mitrāvaruṇav asmad yāvayataṃ pari ||
english: Whatever divine stroke today approaches us seeking to slay — you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, drive it away from us entirely.

sanskrit: itaś cāmutaś cāghaṃ varuṇa yāvaya | vi mahac charma yaccha varīyo yāvayā vadham ||
english: Drive away sin from this side and from that side, O Varuṇa. Spread out great shelter; drive away the stroke — wide protection.

sanskrit: apendra prāco maghavann amitrān apāpāco abhibhūte nudasva | apodīco apa śūrādharāca urau yathā tava śarman madema ||
english: Drive away the eastern enemies, O Indra, O Maghavan; push away the western ones, O conqueror. Drive away the northern ones, drive away those who are lower in the south, so that we may rejoice in your wide shelter.

sanskrit: tena bhūtasya haviṣā punar ā pyāyatām ayam | jāyāṃ yām asmā avidaṃ sā rasenābhi vardhatām ||
english: With that oblation of the existent being, let this man be replenished again. The wife that I have found for him — let her grow abundant with vital sap.

sanskrit: abhi vardhatāṃ prajayā- -abhi rāṣṭreṇa vardhatām | īṣā sahasravīryāv imau stām anupakṣitau ||
english: Let her grow abundant with offspring, let her grow abundant with dominion. May these two be of thousandfold vigor through the yoke-pole — unwasted.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā jāyām ajanayat tvaṣṭāsyai tvāṃ patiṃ dadhau | tvaṣṭā sahasram āyūṃṣi dīrgham āyuḥ kṛṇotu vām ||
english: Tvaṣṭar begot the wife; Tvaṣṭar placed you as husband for her. May Tvaṣṭar make a thousand life-spans, a long life, for you two.

sanskrit: antarikṣeṇa patati viśvā bhūtāvacākaśat | śuno divyasyaitan mahas tasmā etena haviṣā juhomi ||
english: He flies through mid-air, beholding all beings. This is the greatness of the divine dog; for him I pour this oblation.

sanskrit: apsu te janma divi te sadhasthaṃ samudra ātmā mahimā te pṛthivyām | śuno divyasyaitan mahas tasmā etena haviṣā juhomi ||
english: Your birth is in the waters, your dwelling-place is in heaven, your self is the ocean, your greatness is on the earth. This is the greatness of the divine dog; for him I pour this oblation.

sanskrit: ye trayaḥ kālakāñjā divi devā iva śritāḥ | tān sarvān ahva ūtaye 'smā ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: Those three Kālakāñjas who rest in heaven like gods — I call all of them for help, for the unharmed wholeness of this man.

sanskrit: yaḥ puruṣaṃ hūrcchayasi śvā divyo avīrahā | taṃ tvāhaṃ brahmaṇā nude puruṣaṃ mā parā vadhīḥ ||
english: You who cause a man to faint, O divine dog, the killer of menless ones — you I push away with sacred formula. Do not slay this man.

sanskrit: yaḥ piśaṅgo ayodaṃṣṭraḥ śvā divyaḥ pariplavaḥ | tasyāhaṃ nāma jagrabha- -asmā ariṣṭatātaye ayaṃ no jīvatād iti ||
english: The divine dog who is tawny, iron-toothed, and roaming about — his name I have seized, for the unharmed wholeness of this man: "May he live for us," so saying.

sanskrit: ayaṃ no nabhasas patiḥ saṃsphāno abhi rakṣatu | asamātiṃ gṛheṣu naḥ ||
english: May this one, the lord of the sky, Saṃsphāna, protect us — unequaled in our homes.

sanskrit: tvaṃ no nabhasas patir ūrjaṃ gṛheṣu dhāraya | ā puṣṭam etv ā vasu ||
english: You, lord of the sky, sustain nourishing strength in our homes. Let abundance come, let riches come.

sanskrit: deva saṃsphāna sahasrāpoṣasyeśiṣe | tasya no dhehi tasya te bhakṣīmahi tasya te bhaktivāṃso bhūyāsma svāhā ||
english: O god Saṃsphāna, you are the lord of thousandfold nourishment. Grant us a share of it; may we partake of your portion; may we be sharers of your portion. Svāhā!

sanskrit: yantāsi yacchase hastam apa rakṣāṃsi sedhasi | prajāṃ dhanaṃ ca gṛhṇānaḥ parihasto abhūd ayam ||
english: You are a controller, you extend the hand, you drive away the demons. This one has become a wearer of the bracelet, grasping offspring and wealth.

sanskrit: parihasta vi dhāraya yoniṃ garbhāya kartave | maryāde putram ā dhehi taṃ tvam ā gamayāgama ||
english: O bracelet, hold the womb wide open for the making of an embryo. Place a son within the boundary; make him come — come!

sanskrit: yaṃ parihastam abibhar aditiḥ putrakāmyā | tvaṣṭā tam asyā ā badhnād yathā putraṃ suvād iti ||
english: The bracelet that Aditi wore out of longing for a son — Tvaṣṭar has bound that very one onto her, so that she might bring forth a son.

sanskrit: āgacchata āgatasya nāma gṛhṇāmy āyataḥ | indrasya vṛtraghno rājño vāsavasya śatakratoḥ ||
english: Come! Of the one who has come, approaching, I seize the name — of Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, the king, the lord of the Vasus, the performer of a hundred deeds.

sanskrit: yena sūryāṃ sāvitrīm aśvinohatuḥ pathā | tena sam abravīd bhago jāyām ā vahatād iti ||
english: By the path by which the two Aśvins carried Sāvitrī the daughter of the Sun — by that same path Bhaga has spoken: "Let him bring home a wife."

sanskrit: yas te aṅkuśo vasudāno bṛhann indra hiraṇyayaḥ | tenā janīyate jāyāṃ tvaṃ dhehi śatakrato ||
english: Your goad, O Indra, the great one of gold, the giver of goods — with it, place for him who desires a wife his wife, O performer of a hundred deeds.

sanskrit: tvaṃ no medhe prathamā gobhir aśvebhir ā gahi | tvaṃ sūryasya raśmiṣu tvaṃ no asi yajñiyā ||
english: Come to us first, O Intelligence, with cows and horses. You are in the rays of the sun; you are the one worthy of worship for us.

sanskrit: medhām ahaṃ prathamāṃ brahmaṇvatīm ṛṣiṣṭutām | prapītāṃ brahmacāribhir | devānām avasā vṛṇe ||
english: Intelligence, the foremost, full of sacred formulas, praised by seers, drunk deep by those who practice chastity — that intelligence I choose with the help of the gods.

sanskrit: medhāṃ sāyaṃ medhāṃ prātar medhāṃ madhyandinaṃ pari | medhāṃ sūryeṇodyatā- -udīrāṇā u tuṣṭuma ||
english: Intelligence in the evening, intelligence in the morning, intelligence around midday — intelligence rising with the sun, we have praised it as it stirs.

sanskrit: pārthivasya rase devā bhagasya tanvo bale | āyur asmai somo varca ā dhād bṛhaspatiḥ ||
english: In the sap of the earthly one, in the strength of the divine Bhaga's body — Soma has placed life for him, Bṛhaspati has placed brilliance.

sanskrit: āyur asmai dhehi jātavedaḥ prajāṃ tvaṣṭar adhinidhehy ojaḥ | rāyaspoṣaṃ savitar ā suvāsmai śataṃ jīvāti śaradas tavāyam ||
english: Place life for him, O Jātavedas; place offspring and vigor deeply within, O Tvaṣṭar. Press out abundance of riches for him, O Savitṛ. This one of yours shall live a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: āśīr ṇa ūrjam uta suprajāstvaṃ dakṣaṃ dadhātu draviṇaṃ suvarcasam | saṃjayan kṣetrāṇi sahasāham indra kṛṇvāno anyān adharān sapatnān ||
english: May Āśīr grant us nourishment and fine offspring; let it place skill and wealth of bright luster. Conquering fields by might, O Indra, making rivals lower and subdued.

sanskrit: āyam agan savitā kṣureṇa- -uṣṇena vāya udakenehi | ādityā rudrā vasavaḥ sacetasaḥ somasya rājño 'vapan pracetasaḥ ||
english: Savitṛ has come here with the razor, with warm water — come! The Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus, of one mind, the wise ones, have shaved for King Soma.

sanskrit: yenāvapat savitā kṣureṇa somasya rājño varuṇasya vidvān | tena brahmāṇo vapatedam asya- -asrāmo dīrghāyur ayam astu vīraḥ ||
english: With the razor with which Savitṛ, knowing, shaved for King Soma and for Varuṇa — with that razor the brahmin-priests shave this one of his. Let this hero be untired and long-lived.

sanskrit: aditiḥ śmaśru vapatv āpa undantu varcasā | dhārayatu prajāpatiḥ punaḥpunaḥ suvaptave ||
english: Let Aditi shave the beard; let the waters drench him with brilliance. Let Prajāpati hold him again and again for good shaving.

sanskrit: yās te hirā dhamanayo 'ṅgāny anu viṣṭhitāḥ | tāsāṃ te sarvāsāṃ sākaṃ nir viṣāṇi hvayāmasi ||
english: Your arteries and veins that are distributed along your limbs — from all of them together we call forth the poisons out.

sanskrit: yāṃ te rudra iṣum āsthad aṅgebhyo hṛdayāya ca | imāṃ tām adya te vayaṃ viṣūcīṃ vi vṛhāmasi ||
english: The arrow that Rudra has fixed in your limbs and in your heart — that very one today we tear out of you, pointing it away in all directions.

sanskrit: namas te rudrāsyate namaḥ pratihitābhyaḥ | namo visṛjyamānābhyo namas ta āyatābhyaḥ ||
english: Homage to your face, O Rudra, homage to your arrows that are fitted on the bow. Homage to those that are being released; homage to those aimed at us.

sanskrit: avācīḥ pari mūrdhno yās te dhamanayaḥ śatam | tās te pra bhidyantāṃ pṛthag anu tyaṃ lohitāvaṭam ||
english: Your hundred veins that flow downward from the head — let them burst open separately, each following that channel of blood.

sanskrit: syandantāṃ rodanāvatīr anu tyaṃ lohitāvaṭam | yathāsyām antar na raṃsantām anukūlam ivodakam ||
english: Let the ones bearing moisture flow along that channel of blood, so that they may not linger inside him — like water flowing in its course.

sanskrit: pratīcīnaḥ sūrya etu pratīcīḥ sravataḥ kṛtāḥ | avācīs te asnaḥ kulyā iyaṃ tṛṇattv oṣadhīḥ ||
english: Let the sun go westward; the streams made to flow go westward. Let this downward-flowing channel from blood cut through the herbs.

sanskrit: imaṃ yavam aṣṭāyogaiḥ ṣaḍyogebhir acarkṛṣuḥ | sa ghā te tanvo rapaḥ pratīcīnam apa vyayat ||
english: This barley they have plowed with eight teams, with six teams. May it indeed strip away the bodily blemish from you, driving it westward.

sanskrit: nyag vāto vāti nyak tapati sūryaḥ | nīcīnam aghnyā duhe nyag bhavatu te rapaḥ ||
english: The wind blows downward; the sun burns downward. The inviolable cow milks downward. Let your blemish go downward.

sanskrit: āpa id vā u bheṣajīr āpo amīvacātanīḥ | āpaḥ samudrārthā yatīḥ parā vahantu te rapaḥ ||
english: The waters are indeed healers; the waters are the ones that drive away disease. Let the waters, moving toward the ocean, carry your blemish away.

sanskrit: amī ye yudham āyanti ketūn kṛtvānīkaśaḥ | indras tān pary ahār dāmnā tān agne sandyā tvam ||
english: Those who come to battle having made their banners row by row — Indra has bound them around with a cord; you, O Agni, bind them too.

sanskrit: yāvatīḥ sica āyanty anīkāni yati ṣṭan | indras tān pary ahār dāmnā tān agne sandyā tvam ||
english: However many streams come, however many battle-fronts there are — Indra has bound them around with a cord; you, O Agni, bind them too.

sanskrit: saṃ paramān sam avamān atho sandyāni madhyamān | indras tān pary ahār dāmnā tān agne sandyā tvam ||
english: Bind together the farthest ones, bind together the nearest ones, and also bind the middle ones together. Indra has bound them around with a cord; you, O Agni, bind them too.

sanskrit: sandānaṃ vo bṛhaspatiḥ sandānaṃ savitā karat | sandānam indraś cāgniś ca sandānaṃ bhago aśvinā ||
english: Bṛhaspati has made the binding for you, Savitṛ has made the binding. Indra and Agni have made the binding, Bhaga and the two Aśvins have made the binding.

sanskrit: yās te ruco deva sūrya- -udyato divy ātatāḥ | tābhir mām adya sarvābhis tā manuṣyebhyo ruce kṛṇu ||
english: Your radiances, O divine Sun, spread across the sky as you rise — with all of them, make me radiant today before mankind.

sanskrit: ruce mā dhehi brahmasu ruce rājasu dhehi mā | ruce viśyeṣu śūdreṣu mayi dhehi ruce rucim ||
english: Place me in radiance among the brahmin-priests; place me in radiance among the kings. In radiance among the clan-folk and the Śūdras — place radiance in radiance in me.

sanskrit: yā ruco hiraṇye yā agnau yāś ca sūrye | indrāgnī mayi tā ruco ruco dhehi bṛhaspate ||
english: The radiances that are in gold, those that are in Agni, and those that are in the Sun — O Indra and Agni, place those radiances in me. Place radiance upon radiance, O Bṛhaspati.
